content: Ọrụ ubi bụ ọrụ kacha mkpa n’ala Igbo n’oge gboo. Onye anaghị arụ ọrụ ubi ka a na-ele anya ka onye umengwụ. Ihe e ji mara ndị nna anyị hà bụ ịkọ ji, n’ihi na ji bụ eze nri. E nwere ụdị ubi abụọ: ubi dị nso n’ụlọ na ubi dị n’ime ọhịa. Ndị mmadụ na-agba mbọ kọọ ọtụtụ nri ha ga-eri n’afọ niile. Taa, ụmụ ntorobịa anaghị enwe mmasị n’ọrụ ubi. Ha chere na ọ bụ ọrụ ndị ogbenye. Ma n’eziokwu, onye kọrọ nri agaghị enwe agụụ.

questions.q: Gịnị bụ ọrụ kacha mkpa n’ala Igbo n’oge gboo dị ka passage si kwuo?
questions.explanation: The first sentence of the passage states that farming (ọrụ ubi) was the most important work in Igboland in the past.

questions.q: Olee nri a na-akpọ 'eze nri' n'ala Igbo?
questions.explanation: The passage identifies yam (ji) as the 'king of crops' (eze nri).

questions.q: Kedu aha a na-akpọ onye anaghị arụ ọrụ ubi n'oge ahụ?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that someone who doesn't farm is looked upon as a lazy person (onye umengwụ).

questions.q: Gịnị ka ụmụ ntorobịa nke oge a chere banyere ọrụ ubi?
opts: Na ọ bụ ọrụ ndị ọgaranya
Na ọ bụ ọrụ ndị ogbenye
Na ọ bụ ọrụ kacha mma
questions.explanation: The text states that modern youth think farming is a job for poor people.

questions.q: Olee uru ịkọ nri bara dị ka passage si kọwaa?
opts: Agụụ agaghị agụ onye kọrọ nri
questions.explanation: The concluding sentence says that someone who grows food will not go hungry.

q: Mkpụrụedemede asụsụ Igbo dị ole n'ọnụọgụ?
explanation: The Standard Igbo alphabet (Abidịị) consists of 36 letters.

q: Olee n'ime ndị a bụ udaume mfe (Light vowels)?
explanation: The light vowels in Igbo (Udaume mfe) are a, ị, ọ, and ụ.

q: Udaume ole dị n'asụsụ Igbo?
explanation: Igbo language has 8 vowels (udaume).

q: Mgbochiume ole dị n'asụsụ Igbo?
explanation: Out of the 36 letters, 8 are vowels and 28 are consonants (mgbochiume).

q: Olee mkpụrụedemede bụ myiriụda (Nasal consonant acting as a syllable)?
explanation: 'm' and 'n' are nasal sounds that can function as syllables in Igbo words like 'mma' or 'nna'.

q: Ahịrịokwu a 'Obi tiri mkpu' nwere ụdị ngwaa wo?
explanation: 'Tiri' is a transitive verb (Ngwaa mbufe) because the action passes to the object 'mkpu'.

q: Olee akaraolu a na-eji egosi 'Low Tone' n'asụsụ Igbo?
explanation: The low tone is indicated by the grave accent mark (`) on the vowel.

q: Aha nkejiasụsụ na-akọwa aha bụ _____.
explanation: An adjective (Nkọwa) is a word that describes or qualifies a noun.

q: Mgbakwunye na-abịa n'ihu ngwaa bụ _____.
explanation: A prefix is called 'Mbuụzọ' because it comes at the beginning (ihu) of a word root.

q: Mkpụrụokwu 'Akwụkwọ' nwere sillebu ole?
explanation: A-kwụ-kwọ has three syllables.

q: N'ahịrịokwu bụ 'Ada na-eri nri', gịnị bụ 'na-'?
explanation: 'Na' functions as an auxiliary/helping verb (Ngwaa nnyemaka) to show progressive action.

q: Olee akara edemede a na-eji egosi nkwụsị oge na mkparịtaụka?
explanation: A comma (kọma) indicates a short pause in a sentence.

q: Aha obodo bụ 'Enugwu' dabara n'ụdị aha wo?
explanation: Enugwu is a specific name of a place, so it is a proper noun (Aha pụrụ iche).

q: Olee mkpụrụasụsụ a kpọrọ 'Uda-anụ' (Voiced Consonants)?
explanation: Voiced consonants like b, d, g cause vibration in the vocal cords when pronounced.

q: Kpọọ aha nkejiasụsụ na-ejikọ mkpụrụokwu abụọ ọnụ.
explanation: A conjunction (Njikọ) links words or phrases together.

q: N'asụsụ Igbo, 'High tone' anaghị enwe akara ọ bụla n'elu vowel. Eziokwu ka ọ bụ asị?
explanation: In Standard Igbo orthography, the high tone (Udaelu) is typically left unmarked.

q: Olee nke bụ nnọchiaha (Pronoun) n'ime ndị a?
explanation: 'Ha' (They) stands in for a noun, making it a pronoun.

q: Gịnị bụ 'ụdaume mkpuchi' (Heavy vowels)?
explanation: The heavy vowels (udaume mkpuchi/arọ) are e, i, o, and u.

q: Ahịrịokwu a 'Bịa ebe a!' bụ ụdị wo?
explanation: This is an imperative/command sentence (Ahịrịokwu iwu).

q: Onye na-akpụ isi bụ onye _____.
explanation: In Igbo grammar, the person who cuts hair is simply 'onye na-akpụ isi'.

q: Gịnị ka a na-akpọ nwa mụrụ n'ụbọchị 'Eke'?
explanation: A female child born on Eke market day is named Mgbeke.

q: Udaolu ole dị n'asụsụ Igbo?
explanation: Igbo has three tones: High (Elu), Low (Ala), and Mid/Downstep (Nsu).

q: Mkpụrụokwu 'Mmanwụ' nwere mkpụrụedemede ole?
explanation: M-m-a-n-w-ụ consists of 6 letters in the Igbo alphabet (note: double letters like 'nw' are one letter).

q: Kpọọ ngwaa dị n'ahịrịokwu a: 'Nne siri nri'.
explanation: 'Siri' (cooked) is the verb or action word.

q: Gịnị bụ nsonazụ n'ime mkpụrụokwu 'Rie'?
explanation: 'e' is the suffix (nsonazụ) added to the root 'ri'.

q: Olee nke bụ 'mgbochiume kpachịrị akpachị' (Digraph)?
explanation: 'gb' consists of two characters representing one sound, which is a digraph.

q: Ụdị aha 'Nwa' bụ _____.
explanation: 'Nwa' (child) is a common noun (aha nkịtị).

q: Ihe na-abịa n'ihu ngwaa iji mepụta ajụjụ bụ _____.
explanation: Prefixes like 'ọ̀' (e.g., ọ̀ riri?) are used to create questions.

q: Asụsụ Igbo gụnyere 'Udamkpọ' (Vowel Harmony). Gịnị ka ọ pụtara?
opts: Udaume ịbịa n'ìgwè abụọ dị iche
explanation: Vowel harmony means that vowels in a word are usually from the same group (Light or Heavy).

q: Olee onye dere akwụkwọ 'Omenụkọ'?
explanation: Pita Nwana wrote the first Igbo novel, 'Omenụkọ'.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Mbem'?
explanation: Mbem is a form of oral poetry or chant.

q: Olee anụmanụ a maara dị ka onye aghụghọ n'akụkọ ifo Igbo?
explanation: The Tortoise (Mbe) is the archetypal trickster in Igbo folktales.

q: Kammala ilu a: 'Gidi gidi bụ _____.'
explanation: The proverb is 'Gidi gidi bụ ugwu eze', meaning unity/strenuous effort brings honor.

q: Gịnị ka a na-akpọ 'Agụmagụ a kpara akpa'?
explanation: 'Agụmagụ a kpara akpa' refers to creative written literature.

q: Olee onye dere akwụkwọ 'Isi Akwu Dara n'Ala'?
explanation: Tony Ubesie is the author of this classic novel set during the Biafran war.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Figure of Speech' fún 'Personification' n'Igbo?
explanation: Nnyemmadụ (Personification) gives human qualities to non-human entities.

q: Onye bụ nna asụsụ Igbo nke oge a?
explanation: F.C. Ogbalu is widely regarded as the promoter/father of modern Igbo studies.

q: Kedu nke bụ 'Agụmagụ ọnụ'?
explanation: Proverbs and folktales are transmitted orally, hence 'Agụmagụ ọnụ'.

q: Gịnị bụ isiokwu 'Mbem'?
explanation: Mbem usually focuses on praise, history, or prayers/incantations.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Ilu'?
explanation: According to Chinua Achebe, proverbs (ilu) are the palm oil with which words are eaten.

q: Olee ụdị akụkọ na-ezi ezigbo omume ma jiri anụmanụ kọwaa ya?
explanation: Folktales (Akụkọ ifo) use personified animals to teach moral lessons.

q: Kammala ilu a: 'Onye kwe, _____.'
explanation: The proverb is 'Onye kwe, Chi ya ekwe', meaning if you believe, your personal god will support you.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Metaphor' n'asụsụ Igbo?
explanation: Ìfiwé lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ is a direct comparison (metaphor).

q: Olee akwụkwọ e ji amata ụdị agụmagụ 'Novel'?
explanation: All listed are examples of Igbo novels.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Irony' n'asụsụ Igbo?
explanation: Ìfọ̀rọ̀hun-un is the literary term for irony.

q: Agụmagụ 'Egwuregwu' bụ _____.
explanation: 'Egwuregwu' refers to plays or drama meant for performance.

q: Olee onye dere akwụkwọ 'Juọ Obinna'?
explanation: Tony Ubesie wrote 'Juọ Obinna', another famous novel about the civil war.

q: Olee nke kacha mkpa n'ịlụ nwaanyị n'ala Igbo?
explanation: The inquiry/knocking ('Ịjụ ajụjụ') is the essential first step in Igbo marriage.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Ọmụgwọ'?
explanation: Ọmụgwọ is the traditional postpartum care given to a new mother by her mother or a relative.

q: Mmadụ ole na-alụ di na nwunye n'ala Igbo n'oge gboo?
opts: Otu nwoke na otu nwanyị nani
explanation: Historically, polygamy (ịlụ karịa otu nwaanyị) was common and often a sign of wealth/status.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Ego nwaanyị'?
explanation: Bride price is a symbolic token establishing the legal bond between families.

q: Kedu onye bụ onyeisi n'ezinụlọ n'ala Igbo?
explanation: The father (nna) is the traditional head of the household.

q: Mkpụrụ ji ole a tọrọ n'ụdọ ka a na-akpọ _____?
explanation: A barn where yams are tied is called 'Oba'.

q: Olee ememme a na-eme tupu e rie ji ọhụrụ?
explanation: New Yam Festival (Ịwa ji/Iri ji) is done to thank the gods for a successful harvest.

q: Gịnị ka a na-eji amata onye nwere echichi 'Ozo'?
opts: Okpu mme mme na mpị nzu
explanation: Ozo titled men are known by their red caps and elephant tusks.

q: Asụsụ Igbo nwere ụbọchị ahịa ole?
explanation: The Igbo calendar revolves around four market days: Eke, Orie, Afo, and Nkwo.

q: Onye na-ele anya n'ọdịnihu site n'ịgba afa bụ _____.
explanation: A diviner is known as 'Dibia afa'.

q: Gịnị bụ 'Ikwa ozu'?
explanation: 'Ikwa ozu' refers to funeral rites performed to honor the deceased.

q: Onye bụ 'Diọpara'?
explanation: The first-born son is called Diọpara (or Opwara).

q: Olee aha a na-akpọ nwa mbụ nwaanyị mụrụ n'ezinụlọ?
explanation: The first-born daughter is known as 'Ada'.

q: Ịlụ nwanyị n'ala Igbo na-amalite site n'ikụ aka n'ọnụ ụzọ nke a kpọrọ _____.
explanation: The formal introduction/inquiry is called 'Ịjụ ajụjụ'.

q: Gịnị ka 'Oji' na-anọchite anya ya n'ala Igbo?
explanation: Kola nut (Oji) is the ultimate symbol of welcome and peace.

q: Onye na-akpụ ígwè bụ _____.
explanation: A blacksmith is called 'Onye òkpụ ígwè'.

q: Ịgba mgba n'ala Igbo bụ _____.
explanation: Traditional wrestling (Ịgba mgba) is a sport used to test strength.

q: Gịnị bụ uru 'Ịmụ ọrụ' (Apprenticeship)?
opts: Ịmụta aka ọrụ na inwe onwe
explanation: The apprenticeship system helps youth learn trades and become independent.

q: N'ala Igbo, 'Iru mgbede' bụ ememme a na-emere _____.
explanation: 'Iru mgbede' was a rite of passage for young women entering adulthood/marriage.

q: Kedu onye n'obodo na-ahụ maka ikpe ikpe na idozi okwu?
opts: Ndị Nze na Ọzo na ndị okenye
explanation: Titled men and elders (Oha na Eze/Ndi Ichie) handle conflict resolution.
